concept: macOS vm pressure level thresholds kVMPressureWarning and kVMPressureCritical
summary: Definitions: `AVAILABLE_NON_COMPRESSED_MEMORY` = active + inactive + free + speculative pages (N); `VM_PAGE_COMPRESSOR_COUNT` = resident pages of the compressor object (C, "Pages occupied by compressor" in vm_stat); `AVAILABLE_MEMORY` = N + C.

facts.text: Definitions: `AVAILABLE_NON_COMPRESSED_MEMORY` = active + inactive + free + speculative pages (N); `VM_PAGE_COMPRESSOR_COUNT` = resident pages of the compressor object (C, "Pages occupied by compressor" in vm_stat); `AVAILABLE_MEMORY` = N + C.
Normal to Warning (compressor active): N < VM_PAGE_COMPRESSOR_COMPACT_THRESHOLD = AVAILABLE_MEMORY x 10 / minorcompact_divisor.
On macOS with more than 3 GB of RAM the divisors are minorcompact 20, majorcompact 25, unthrottle 35, catchup 50; with 3 GB or less they are 11, 13, 20, 35.
So for a Mac above 3 GB, Normal to Warning fires when N < (N + C) x 10/20, that is N < C. Derived.
Warning to Critical: `vm_compressor_low_on_space()` OR N < 1.2 x AVAILABLE_MEMORY x 10 / 35. That is about N < 0.52 C. Derived.
Hysteresis, down: Warning to Normal needs N > 1.2 x the warning threshold, which is N > 0.6 (N + C), about N > 1.5 C. Critical to Warning needs N > 1.4 x the unthrottle threshold, about N > 0.67 C.

If the compressor is not active the thresholds are page-count based: warning below `memorystatus_get_soft_memlimit_page_shortage_threshold`, critical below the critical page shortage threshold, and recovery needs 115 percent of the threshold.

The non-compressor percentages (iOS style) are listed in kern_memorystatus.c by DRAM size: 6 GB and up is critical 4 percent, idle 8, pressure 12, reaper 16, freeze 50; 0 to 3 GB is 5, 10, 15, 20, 50. On a compressor-active Mac these are not what drives the level.
`vm_pressure_response` also sets `memorystatus_level` = available x 100 / total pages (the sysctl `kern.memorystatus_level`), but the level transitions above do not use that percentage.
The level re-broadcasts after sitting in a non-normal level for 30 minutes (`vm_pressure_level_transition_threshold`).

Measured: N was 1,910,295 pages and C was 746,105 pages (N/C about 2.56) with `kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level` = 1 (Normal) and `kern.memorystatus_level` = 46 at the same moment, consistent with the N versus C rule. [asserted] (measured locally 2026-10-04, Apple M5 Max 64 GB, macOS 27.2; vm_stat, sysctl)
Not documented in sources read.

Wired memory (1,477,245 pages on the measured host) is excluded from N, so a large wired GPU allocation shrinks N without growing C, and the Warning line N < C is reached when active + inactive + free fall below the compressor's own footprint.
`kern.memorystatus_level` can read 46 percent while pressure is Normal and a "low" percentage does not imply Warning.
The Warning line moves as C grows: heavy compression raises C and so raises the N needed to stay Normal.

Common folklore ties the Activity Monitor memory-pressure colors to a free-percentage (for example 10 percent / 5 percent). The source read shows a compressor-relative rule on macOS instead. No Apple document confirming the folklore percentages was found.
The numeric enum values of kVMPressureUrgent and kVMPressureCritical were not found in the files read.
Whether VM_CONFIG_COMPRESSOR_IS_ACTIVE is true on every Apple silicon Mac build; macOS defaults to compressor-with-swap, so it should be.
The long-run behavior of Activity Monitor's graph versus this level.
On Macs above 3 GB the Warning threshold is N < C (non-compressed available pages below the compressor's resident pages).
Critical is low-on-space or N below about half of C.
Hysteresis uses 120 percent (warning to normal) and 140 percent (critical to warning) multipliers.
The compressor divisors differ for 3 GB or less versus larger Macs.
A stuck non-normal level re-notifies every 30 minutes.
